buttonLabel: "Discover nature in Venezuela and Bolivia"
lead: >-
  Venezuela and Bolivia reveal nature at opposite elevations on our 12-day itinerary. The Caribbean islands of Los Roques, Canaima Lagoon and Angel Falls give way to the Uyuni Salt Flat, Incahuasi Island and a chain of Andean lagoons. Birdwatching opportunities are concentrated in Bolivia's highlands. Sea turtles and additional island trips in Los Roques are listed separately and are not automatically included in the basic tour.
---

## Two countries, two completely different natural worlds

[Venezuela](/venezuela/) begins by the Caribbean Sea and continues through Canaima's forests and waterfalls. In [Bolivia](/bolivia/), the route climbs to La Paz, the white expanse of Uyuni and the Altiplano's lagoons. Comparing the countries merely as places with "beautiful landscapes" is not enough: altitude, temperature, transport and opportunities to observe animals all change.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The featured product is [“Nature and Culture of Venezuela and Bolivia in 12 Days”](/multi-country/tour/venezuela-bolivia-nature-culture-12-days/). Specific days are devoted to natural attractions, but the trip also includes city walks and cultural excursions. It does not promise a specialized rare-species safari or prolonged wildlife-research expedition.

| Venezuela | Bolivia |
|---|---|
| Caribbean islands and tropical lagoons | Salt flat and high-altitude lagoons |
| Local curiara boats and forest trails | Overland trips to geysers and lakes |
| Marine environment and tepuis | Flamingos, vicuñas and other Andean wildlife |

## Los Roques: Caribbean islands and optional wildlife encounters

On days two and three, travelers fly from Caracas to the [Los Roques archipelago](/venezuela/place/los-roques/). The main itinerary provides time to relax on the islands of Madrisquí or Francisquí, enjoy the beaches and swim. Guests are supplied with loungers and packed lunches with drinks. This island stage contrasts sharply with the Bolivian conditions later in the trip.

Los Roques is associated with marine ecosystem conservation. Distinguishing included activities from optional ones is essential. Trips to more distant islands, a visit to a sea turtle conservation station, a natural pool with starfish and boat fishing are listed as **additional options**. Promising a guaranteed turtle encounter or treating a fishing outing as included would therefore be incorrect.

Travelers choosing the trip for marine animals should first decide what sort of experience they want: observation from shore, a boat excursion or a dedicated program with qualified guidance. [Wildlife trips in Latin America](/interests/wildlife/) offer more formats; this itinerary combines a marine holiday with other landscapes and countries.

## Canaima and Angel Falls: the nature of the tepuis

After returning to Caracas, the group flies to [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/). UNESCO describes the national park as a region of distinctive table-top tepui mountains, sheer cliffs and cascades. For visitors, this is an area where water transport matters: local curiara boats navigate Canaima Lagoon and the Carrao River.

On day four, the route crosses the lagoon beside several waterfalls, with an island walk and a passage behind the curtain of El Sapo Falls. Day five is devoted to the major trip to Angel Falls: a motorboat journey, forest crossing and a walk of approximately one hour to a viewpoint. Day six is reserved for rest beside the lagoon. Flights above the falls, kayaks and separate hikes are offered as extras.

The main result is discovering tepui geology, forest, rivers and waterfalls. No separate list of bird or mammal species to be observed at Canaima is provided, so it would be misleading to advertise a guaranteed photographic safari featuring particular animals. Access to boat routes and trails is checked for the selected dates and water conditions.

## Uyuni: salt, cacti and a change of scenery

After the Caracas–La Paz flight, the Bolivia stage begins. On day nine, the group flies to the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The route passes Colchani village, the so-called salt eyes in the salt crust and [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/). Guests can walk among large cacti and enjoy a broad panorama of the white plain.

Visitors sometimes imagine Uyuni only as a mirror after rain. In reality, dry salt and seasonal surface water create different versions of the same landscape. The program includes a sunset visit to the salt flat, but cannot guarantee a reflective surface in every kind of weather. When choosing dates, we help relate photographic expectations to seasonal conditions and access to individual areas.

This day is primarily about landforms, salt formations and cacti. The principal birdwatching opportunities come later at southwestern Bolivia's smaller lagoons.

## High-altitude lagoons, flamingos and vicuñas

On day ten, the journey passes the Valley of Rocks and the Cañapa, Hedionda, Chiar Khota and Honda lagoons. Flamingos and other birds may be seen here. The following day goes through the Siloli Desert, the Stone Tree, [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), thermal springs and Sol de Mañana geysers, then crosses the Dalí Desert to [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) beneath Licancabur Volcano.

Around the Eduardo Avaroa reserve, the program allows for possible encounters with vicuñas and wild foxes. Such sightings depend on the animals and conditions on the day. **Including a location in the itinerary does not guarantee an encounter with a particular species.** Binoculars and time to stop calmly where permitted can help.

| Natural site | What to look for |
|---|---|
| Small lagoons | Flamingos and other birds |
| Laguna Colorada | A high-altitude lake and landscape |
| Sol de Mañana | Geothermal activity |
| Laguna Verde | A lake beneath Licancabur Volcano |

This stage includes an overnight stay at approximately 4,400 meters; the geyser visit reaches nearly 5,000 meters. Warm clothes, sun and wind protection are essential. Discuss the risk of altitude sickness even if you are physically fit, and agree with a doctor on appropriate acclimatization measures before the trip.

## When to go and how to pack for two climates

Venezuela's warm Caribbean islands and Bolivia's cold highlands require different luggage. For Los Roques and Canaima, lightweight clothes, sun protection, waterproof packing for boat journeys and shoes for wet trails matter. In Bolivia, bring layers, a warm jacket, a hat and comfortable closed-toe shoes. Sunlight reflects strongly off the bright salt surface, and Altiplano temperatures fall quickly after sunset.

A flight links the countries, while the high-altitude section uses ground transport through remote regions. Road conditions, weather, potential restrictions in natural areas and spare time are important to the entire sequence. Avoid arranging a tight independent flight connection immediately after a long outing to the lagoons.

Entry requirements for Venezuela and Bolivia, transit through other countries, passport validity and official safety advisories must be checked for each nationality and departure date. For the Venezuela stage, evaluating current regional restrictions and insurance coverage is particularly important. Payments use different national currencies, so agree on workable payment methods for each stage rather than making universal promises about card acceptance.

## Who will enjoy this nature program

This route is best suited to travelers wishing to see **the sea, a tropical national park, a salt flat and high-altitude lagoons** on one trip. It also includes urban and cultural stops that provide a break from long nature outings. Anyone whose sole goal is a birdwatching expedition, specialist sea turtle observation or scuba diving would need a different allocation of days and separately confirmed services.

Compare the actual contents of [Venezuela tours](/venezuela/tour/) and [Bolivia itineraries](/bolivia/tour/), including duration and included outings. On the current 12-day product, **the international flight between Caracas and La Paz is excluded from the basic package**, despite domestic flights within each country being included.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_priroda_i_kultura_venesuely_bolivii}}

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Venezuela and Bolivia

### Can we see flamingos on this trip?

Yes, the route passes several Bolivian lagoons where the itinerary anticipates flamingo watching. Actual encounters depend on the season, weather and bird behavior, so no specific number is guaranteed.

### Is the sea turtle conservation station on Los Roques included?

No. It is listed among optional island activities. The core program includes relaxing on Madrisquí or Francisquí beaches with packed lunches.

### Is there a hike to Angel Falls?

Yes. The outing combines a motorboat and approximately one hour walking through forest to a viewpoint. Bring shoes suitable for an uneven wet trail and be prepared for a long excursion day.

### Which stage reaches the highest elevations?

Southwestern Bolivia's lagoons and geysers, with an overnight stay around 4,400 meters and some stops nearing 5,000 meters. Discuss altitude preparation and flexibility in pacing before departure.

buttonLabel: "Explore journeys through Brazil and Chile"
lead: >-
  Brazil and Chile reveal two very different sides of South America: Rio de Janeiro's ocean beaches and Iguazu Falls, followed by Santiago, the Pacific coast or the Atacama Desert. The countries do not share a border, and Argentina is an important stop on many current itineraries. To choose the right journey, check not only the country list but also flight order, entry rules for every destination, climate differences and which services are actually included.
---

## Brazil and Chile in one journey: what to know before choosing a tour

**A Brazil–Chile itinerary is usually an extended South American journey, not a simple transfer between neighboring countries.** Brazil is on the Atlantic and Chile on the Pacific; they have no shared land border. Major stops may be thousands of kilometers apart and involve connections at different airports. The aim when choosing a tour is to preserve time for the experiences rather than spend most of the holiday traveling.

Here we feature {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with both countries among the **principal destinations**. This is a selection criterion, not a guarantee that the route visits only two countries. Argentina is also important on current itineraries: via [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and the [Argentine side of Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), travelers visit a third country with its own immigration rules and currency.

A classic combination runs through [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), Buenos Aires and [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). Longer options add Chile's Atacama Desert, wine valleys, Patagonia or other regions. The order of cities depends on flights, dates and the specific tour program.

To begin, compare three of our tours:

- [Brazil, Argentina and Chile with Iguazu in 12 Days](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-iguazu-12-days/): Rio, both sides of the falls, Buenos Aires and Santiago.
- [“Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama”](/multi-country/tour/sun-tango-wine-atacama/): the same major cities and Iguazu, with an extension to San Pedro de Atacama.
- [“New Year Fairy Tale: Brazil, Argentina and Chile”](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/): a separate group tour celebrating New Year on Copacabana at the turn of 2026–2027.

| Program | Main difference |
|---|---|
| 12 days with Iguazu | Cities, ocean, waterfalls |
| 15 days with Atacama | Desert and highlands |
| New Year 2027 | A festive trip on fixed dates |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_solntse_tango_i_vino,tour_source_solntse_tango_vino_i_atakama,tour_brazil_argentina_chile_new_year_11_days_2027}}

## Connecting the Atlantic, Iguazu and the Pacific

Rio de Janeiro is a natural place to begin an extended journey: after a long-haul flight, travelers can see the city from Sugarloaf Mountain, ascend to Christ the Redeemer and spend time by the ocean. The route can then continue to Iguazu, where nature offers a very different experience.

The falls form a single river system, but they are visited through **two national parks in different countries**. The Brazilian side near [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) provides sweeping panoramas of the cascades. From [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), paths take visitors closer to individual falls. A border crossing, park hours and driving time must be accounted for. Mentioning "Iguazu" in a tour does not establish that both sides are included: check the day-by-day schedule.

[Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) is often the next stop, shifting the journey from nature to architecture and tango. From there, the itinerary continues to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), a city at the foot of the Andes with its own culture and geography.

Chile provides several possible extensions. Some tours add [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/) on the Pacific coast. Others continue from Santiago to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) for salt flats, desert valleys and high-altitude lagoons. These options differ in duration, flights and physical demands.

**Rio's ocean beaches, Iguazu Falls and Chile's high-altitude regions require different luggage and daily schedules.** The more natural zones you want to include, the more carefully the travel sequence must be designed.

## Why you should not plan flights from a map alone

Two airports appearing close together on a map do not automatically offer a convenient connection. On Brazil–Chile journeys, distinguish the airport, city and country of each leg.

Rio's international Galeão airport has code **GIG**, while the city airport Santos Dumont is **SDU**. Near Iguazu, Brazil's airport is **IGU** and Argentina's is **IGR**, on opposite sides of the border. In Buenos Aires, international Ezeiza (**EZE**) and Aeroparque (**AEP**) are also in different locations; changing between them requires ground transport. Santiago's principal international airport is **SCL**.

If Atacama follows Santiago, travelers usually look for flights to the Calama area followed by an overland transfer to San Pedro. Assess the journey **from hotel to hotel**, not only time in the air. On separate tickets, passengers may need to collect baggage, check in again and pass immigration.

When arranging a program, we coordinate the city sequence, ground transfers and sensible connection buffers. A long international flight, visits to both sides of Iguazu and a transfer to Chile's natural areas should not be packed thoughtlessly into one day.

Also consider **transit countries** on the journey to South America. Their visa rules depend on nationality, the airport, whether flights are on one or several tickets and whether passengers leave the transit area. Even a journey featuring three South American countries may need a fourth document check for a connecting airport.

## Visas and entry: check the actual three countries

For **Russian citizens holding ordinary valid passports and traveling for short-term tourism**, visa-free travel agreements apply to Brazil and Chile. According to official information, Russian tourists may stay in each country for up to **90 days within a 180-day period**, under the respective agreement. Terms apply separately to each country.

If a tour enters Argentina, its rules must be checked independently. Russia and Argentina also have an agreement for short-term visa-free tourism, up to 90 days within a 180-day period. **Visa-free entry into one country does not replace documents for another**, and permission to connect in an airport without a visa does not confer an unrestricted transit right.

Rules can differ for other nationalities, travel with children, extended stays or non-tourist purposes. Check passport validity, border procedures, onward or return travel evidence, financial means and health coverage for the exact itinerary. If entering a country several times, count days already used.

Chile has the **Permanencia Transitoria** immigration category for short visits. Immigration authorities determine the permitted stay; keep proof of entry. Chile's SAG agricultural authority also requires declaring products of plant or animal origin at the border. This is easy to overlook after Argentina: food carried for personal use is also subject to checks.

We help create a document checklist for each nationality and travel sequence, clarify transit and align the route with these requirements. The final admission decision belongs to border authorities and cannot be guaranteed by a tour operator.

## Three currencies: the real, Argentine peso and Chilean peso

Brazil uses the **Brazilian real (BRL)** and Chile the **Chilean peso (CLP)**. When Argentina is included, a third currency appears, the **Argentine peso (ARS)**. The shared word "peso" does not imply a shared exchange rate or payment system.

Planning every expense in US dollars is risky. USD may be useful for exchange or certain tourist services, but everyday purchases and local transport often require local currency. Rates, ATM fees and cash acceptance vary, so one universal exchange rate for three countries is inappropriate.

For holders of Russian-issued bank cards, there is a specific restriction: **Visa and Mastercard cards issued by Russian banks do not work outside Russia on the respective international networks**. If you rely on a foreign bank card, check transaction availability in Brazil, Argentina and Chile, terminal restrictions and fees with its issuer. Simply possessing a card does not guarantee acceptance in all three countries.

Before departure, separate spending into services already paid for under the selected tour contract and expenses paid on site. For the latter, check the local currency and available payment methods. We help distinguish program payments and suggest what payment arrangements to verify, but do not promise currency exchange, acceptance of a particular bank's card or a fixed exchange rate.

## Brazilian heat, Chilean Atacama and travel seasons

Brazil and Chile do not share one ideal travel month. Rio's climate differs even from Brazil's inland areas and Amazonia. In Chile, traveling from the central region toward the high-altitude desert also changes temperatures and packing requirements.

### Rio and Iguazu

Rio is warm year-round, with Southern Hemisphere summer, roughly December through February, often hot and humid. Iguazu may experience heavy rains and high humidity in warmer months. Walks near the falls usually require shoes suitable for wet paths and light rain protection. Water levels can affect access to individual viewpoints.

For a holiday-centered trip, the event date is the main constraint. For example, the [Copacabana New Year itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/) is set for a specific departure crossing from 2026 into 2027. Its schedule cannot be moved to another month without altering the product.

### Santiago and the Pacific coast

In [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), summer is generally dry and warm, while winter is cooler and wetter. On a trip to [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/), proximity to the Pacific changes how the temperature feels. Clothes for a city excursion and an evening oceanfront walk may differ even on the same day.

### San Pedro de Atacama and the highlands

Near [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), dry desert landscapes meet high-altitude regions. Sunshine can be very intense during the day, with temperatures dropping after sunset. Trips to lagoons, salt flats and geysers require warm layers, UV protection and appropriate pacing because of elevation.

Between December and March, parts of the northern Chilean Altiplano experience summer precipitation sometimes called the **“Bolivian winter.”** It can affect mountain roads and access to some attractions. This does not mean all of Atacama becomes rainy: conditions vary by location, altitude and date. Discuss personal health and contraindications with a doctor before high-altitude excursions, especially if you have heart or lung conditions.

If Atacama is your priority, choose the season and order of highland outings before fixing beach days in Rio. If New Year or Carnival in Brazil is the main objective, set event dates first, then examine weather during the Chile stage.

## Health and luggage: different requirements in two countries

For Brazilian beaches, bring light clothes, a hat and sun protection. For Iguazu walks, non-slip shoes and water protection will be useful. High-altitude outings in Chile require additional warm layers, a windproof jacket, sunglasses and skin protection.

Parts of the journey are at very different elevations. In [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) and on Altiplano excursions, do not assume you will feel the same as at sea level in Rio. Altitude and cold increase preparation needs. Compare the actual excursions: viewpoint stops, long hikes and remote highland trips have different restrictions.

For some Brazilian regions, doctors may recommend vaccination against yellow fever depending on the route, vaccination history and individual contraindications. It would be wrong to declare this automatically mandatory for every tourist entering Brazil or Chile. Health preparations and possible transit-country requirements must be checked against the actual itinerary.

Baggage limits on international and domestic flights may differ within the same journey. Pack layers, check suitcase weight in advance and keep things needed during changing weather accessible.

## Which Ada Tours itinerary should you choose?

**For a first South American journey without a high-altitude stage**, begin with the [12-day tour of Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires and Santiago](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-iguazu-12-days/). It contrasts the ocean, waterfalls and two capitals while remaining shorter than expedition-style programs.

To see northern Chile's desert, lagoons and mountains, consider [“Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama”](/multi-country/tour/sun-tango-wine-atacama/). Extra flights and high-altitude excursions require more time and different luggage. This is particularly appropriate for travelers who value contrasting natural landscapes over several extra days of free time at the ocean.

For a fixed celebration, there is the [2027 New Year itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/). Check exact dates, group arrangements, accommodation and excursion terms first. Adding [Patagonia](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) or [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/) creates different logistics, more flights and more days. Compare those trips by their actual programs rather than the general phrase "Brazil and Chile."

We help choose the sequence of countries, coordinate transfers, clarify required document checks and select a pace that suits the trip's goals. The confirmed services, from guides to domestic flights, are determined by the chosen tour. **A multi-country catalog does not mean all tours include identical hotels, insurance or excursions.**

## Frequently asked questions

### Can we visit only Brazil and Chile, without Argentina?

This is geographically possible, but current programs in this selection include routes where Argentina is also a principal country. Check the full country list and itinerary of the chosen tour. A trip strictly limited to two countries needs a separately agreed route and terms.

### Do Russians need one visa for Brazil, Chile and Argentina?

There is no single visa covering all three. Separate visa-free agreements apply to ordinary Russian passport holders on short tourist trips, generally up to 90 days within 180 days in each country under its own rules. Check transit countries, purpose and passport validity separately.

### Where should we connect between Brazil and Chile?

It depends on the actual flights and stops. Argentina is important on many ready-made routes. The Iguazu area has two airports in different countries, IGU and IGR; in Buenos Aires, distinguish EZE from AEP. Consider border crossings, baggage collection and airport transfers as well as flights.

### Can we pack the same clothes for Rio and Atacama?

Light clothes are enough for many oceanfront walks, but Chile's highlands can be cold even in warm seasons. Bring warm layers, a windproof jacket, closed shoes and sun protection, adjusting the list for month, altitude and excursions.

### Which currency should we bring?

Brazil uses reais, Chile Chilean pesos and Argentina Argentine pesos. Dollars can be useful for exchange but do not replace local payment methods. Russian-issued Visa and Mastercard cards do not work on international networks abroad; check foreign-issued cards ahead of time.

### Should we choose Iguazu or Atacama if time is limited?

With a short holiday, select your main nature attraction and allow time to experience it. Iguazu fits well between Rio and Buenos Aires. Atacama generally requires additional flights and days for high-altitude excursions; a very short program attempting to include everything may be too demanding.

lead: >-
  An adventure route through Brazil and Chile moves between the tropical coast and the Andes. Brazil's stages include Rio and Iguazu, while Chile offers high-altitude Atacama, desert lagoons or windy Patagonia. The main decision is which nature regions the chosen itinerary actually includes and how much time flights and acclimatization require.

## Brazil and Chile: adventures across several natural regions

**Combining Brazil and Chile is appealing because of their contrasts in altitude, humidity and landscape.** In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the ocean meets granite mountains and Tijuca Forest. Near [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), trails pass through humid subtropical nature. Chile offers different experiences: [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) serves as a base for desert valleys and high-altitude outings, while the [Torres del Paine region](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) reveals Patagonia's lakes, mountains and strong winds.

Brazil and Chile do not share a land border. Consequently, a journey "from one country to the other" often involves flights or a route through other countries. Check the complete sequence of countries and cities rather than assuming that two names on a page represent a simple short transfer.

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} in which Brazil and Chile are principal countries and adventure is a substantial theme. That does not promise climbing, rafting and multi-day trekking on every tour. The actual activities are defined by the day-by-day descriptions.

## What to choose: Atacama or Patagonia

[Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) appeals to travelers seeking a dry desert, salt flats, unusual rock formations and landscapes high in the Andes. Some nature stops on outings from San Pedro are at considerable altitude. Even by bus or car, physical demands may differ from ordinary sightseeing at sea level. Early departures, strong sunshine, dryness and cold mornings also affect comfort.

[Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) is chosen for mountains and glacial scenery. Distinguish a panoramic vehicle trip with viewpoint stops from a long hiking route. Park trails have their own weather, access and equipment requirements. According to CONAF, specific winter trail restrictions applied in 2026, and tickets and access conditions should be checked through the park's official system.

A long journey may include both Atacama and Patagonia as well as Brazil's waterfalls for maximum contrast. With limited time, it is usually more practical to choose one Chilean nature region and reserve days for Rio or Iguazu.

| Chilean region | Main characteristic |
|---|---|
| Atacama | Desert and altitude |
| Torres del Paine | Mountains and wind |
| Santiago | Urban stop |

## Current tours and how they differ

The [Chile and Argentina Grand Tour with Iguazu in Brazil](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) connects Easter Island, Atacama, Torres del Paine, El Calafate, Mendoza, Iguazu and Buenos Aires. This is a packed journey with three principal countries, including several Chilean nature regions.

The [five-country group tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) goes from Rio and Iguazu to Santiago, Atacama, Bolivia's highlands and Peru. Its adventure component comes from experiencing different geographic zones, including road travel across the Andean plateau.

The [extended eight-country program](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) covers even more destinations, but needs considerable time. Compare days in each country, early flights and transfers with connections.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_chile_argentina_private_grand_tour_17_days,tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The [full Brazil and Chile selection](/multi-country/brazil_chile/) also includes cultural and food-and-wine itineraries. [Multi-country adventure programs](/multi-country/interests/adventure/) allow comparison with other country combinations sharing this interest.

## When to travel and how to pack

Rio and Iguazu are more humid and warm, while Chilean Andean temperatures depend on elevation and time of day. Atacama's daytime sunshine contrasts with cool mornings. Patagonia calls for a windproof jacket and warm layers even in Southern Hemisphere summer.

A practical kit across these regions includes sun protection, a hat, light rain gear, warm clothes and shoes with reliable grip. Specialist equipment depends on the actual activity: established viewpoints require different preparation from a serious trek.

Chilean Patagonia is generally more convenient for many overland visits in the warmer Southern Hemisphere months, while Atacama's highlands have other weather limitations. Choose the season according to the stage motivating the whole journey, then check the other destinations. Do not apply Rio's "summer" weather to Chile's high-altitude areas.

## Documents, health and connections

According to Brazilian embassy information current on October 16, 2026, ordinary Russian passport holders may enter Brazil visa-free for short tourist stays of up to 90 days within 180 days. Chile uses the short-stay Permanencia Transitoria category, generally up to 90 days, but advance authorization rules depend on nationality. Check the particular Russian passport, itinerary and transit requirements before buying flights. Argentina, Bolivia and Peru apply their own rules when visited.

Chile's SAG agricultural controls require plant- and animal-origin products to be declared at entry. This matters when flying with edible souvenirs or products brought from a previous country.

Altitude is primarily an issue in Atacama and the Andean highlands. Allow reasonable acclimatization and consider medical contraindications before high-altitude days. Protection against yellow fever may also be relevant for some Brazilian regions. Document and health requirements depend on actual destinations, not just country names.

Brazil uses the real, Chile the Chilean peso, and currency changes again in intermediate countries. Russian-issued cards on international payment networks should not be treated as a universal payment method. We help clarify prepaid services and local expenses, but acceptance of a particular card or exchange method must be confirmed independently.

## Choosing a comfortable level of difficulty

Compare more than the number of countries: ask about excursion altitudes, daily distances, transport type, connection times and overnight stays between early departures. A difficult mountain day directly after a long-haul flight may be unwise. For families traveling with children or anyone with physical limitations, choose outings with appropriate conditions.

Compare current country-specific offerings in [Brazil adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/brazil/) and [Chile adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/chile/). They show which stages genuinely belong to available tours and which would be separate optional additions.

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Brazil and Chile

### Can we drive directly from Brazil to Chile?

The countries share no border, so an overland route passes through another country and can be very long. On extended tourist programs, actual flights and connections are usually more important.

### Are Torres del Paine hiking trails included?

Only when specified in a particular itinerary day. Touring the park by vehicle with viewpoint stops and undertaking a sporting trek have different conditions.

### How does Atacama differ from Iguazu in physical demands?

At Iguazu the main factors are humidity, heat and walking; Atacama's high-altitude sections involve thinner air, dryness and temperature variation. Preparation and equipment differ accordingly.

### How many countries will the selected tour visit?

Both named countries are principal destinations in this selection, but many programs also cover three, five or eight countries. Check the complete route and actual overnight stays before booking.

## Beach holidays in Brazil and Chile: what the tour actually includes

[Brazil](/brazil/) and [Chile](/chile/) have long ocean coastlines, but our itinerary differs from a typical beach vacation. It passes through both countries, with the sea and beaches occupying only selected parts of the trip.

This themed selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}, centered on the [“Chile and Argentina: 17-Day Grand Tour with Iguazu in Brazil”](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/). This private journey includes Easter Island, Atacama, Patagonia, Mendoza and Iguazu Falls. Anakena Beach on Easter Island is a stop during an excursion day. **Rio de Janeiro, Búzios and other Brazilian beach resorts are not included in this tour.**

## Anakena: a beach among the monuments of Rapa Nui

[Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/) is a Chilean island territory in the Pacific Ocean. The itinerary devotes three travel days to it, including arrival and return flights. Initial excursions visit Rano Kau Volcano and the ceremonial village of Orongo, then important Rapa Nui archaeological sites.

Day four includes Ahu Akahanga, the Rano Raraku quarry, Ahu Tongariki with its restored moai and other monuments. At the end of the day, the group heads to [Anakena Beach](/chile/place/anakena-beach/) and the Ahu Nau Nau platform. The itinerary allows time to swim and relax after the sightseeing activities.

Anakena combines pale sand, the ocean and nearby ceremonial structures. UNESCO lists Rapa Nui National Park as a World Heritage Site for its Polynesian cultural heritage and moai. Archaeological visits are subject to site rules; visitors must not leave permitted paths or approach monuments where prohibited.

The essential point is understanding how much beach time is available. **This is one stop within a sightseeing day, not a multi-day stay at an ocean resort.** The itinerary also includes long flights between the island and Santiago, so extra beach days cannot be added without changing the travel schedule.

## Why Brazil means Iguazu here rather than beaches

The Brazil stage occupies days 13–15. A private flight takes guests from Mendoza to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), where accommodation is at Belmond Hotel das Cataratas. The program then includes the Brazilian side of the waterfalls, Macuco Safari and the Bird Park. The next day moves to Iguazu's Argentine side and continues to Buenos Aires.

Iguazu lies inland. Its main attractions are waterfalls and tropical forest in the national park. The included boat portion of Macuco Safari brings guests onto the river close to the falls, but **this is a river excursion at the waterfalls, not beach swimming or an Atlantic Ocean holiday**.

If the main purpose is combining Chilean beaches with a Brazilian seaside resort, the existing 17-day product would need redesigning. Discuss time on [Brazil's coast](/brazil/) or browse the [full Brazil tour catalog](/brazil/tour/) instead of expecting a beach holiday not included in the itinerary.

## What else fills the 17-day grand tour

Rapa Nui is just one part of this long journey. The opening days cover Santiago and the Millahue wine region. After Easter Island, travelers return to Chile's capital, fly to Atacama, visit the Valley of the Moon and then move to Patagonia. The Torres del Paine day includes lakes, Salto Grande waterfall and other natural attractions.

Next come Argentina's [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), Perito Moreno Glacier, Mendoza wineries, both sides of Iguazu and Buenos Aires neighborhoods with a tango show. In this combination, Anakena Beach is a peaceful interlude between cultural sightseeing, flights and nature trips.

Separate snorkeling, scuba diving, surfing instructors and sea cruises on Easter Island are not part of the mandatory program. A beach stop does not imply that every water sport is included. If you want an active marine holiday, the activities and safety requirements must be agreed as a separate product.

## When to plan swimming on Easter Island

Easter Island is in the Pacific and has conditions unlike mainland Chile. Swimming depends on season, wind, waves, water temperature and local instructions. Since Anakena is visited within a busy sightseeing day, even favorable weather does not turn it into a full free day.

Pack lightweight beach clothes, a quick-drying towel, sun protection and shoes suitable for archaeological sites. Other stages need warm and windproof clothing: Atacama and Patagonia are very different. It would be a mistake to pack for the entire journey as if it were a beach holiday.

A Rapa Nui visit requires checking the current island entry rules, accommodation reservation and national park visit requirements. These differ from simply moving within a major city and should be confirmed for the dates and nationality.

## Brazil and Chile: what makes this cultural combination worthwhile

**Brazil and Chile provide a contrast between Atlantic urban culture and the Pacific coast.** In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), travelers explore historic neighborhoods and a city shaped by mountains, bay and ocean. In [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the introduction begins in a historic city center at the foot of the Andes.

[Valparaíso](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/) adds another dimension: a historic port built on steep hillsides. Some longer itineraries also include [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/), where Rapa Nui cultural monuments survive. These places belong to different eras and regions, so Chile cannot be reduced to a single Santiago sightseeing tour.

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Brazil and Chile among the principal countries and a culture-and-history theme. **Many tours include Argentina as a full third stage.** The two-country filter does not imply a direct bilateral journey. A broader selection without the theme is available in the [Brazil + Chile catalog](/multi-country/brazil_chile/).

## Rio: nature as part of urban history

In Rio, the city and its natural surroundings are particularly closely connected. [Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and Sugarloaf Mountain provide views over the bay and neighborhoods, while a tour of the historic center introduces another side of Brazil's past. UNESCO has listed Rio's cultural landscapes between mountain and sea as World Heritage, recognizing the relationship among nature, architecture and everyday city life.

The [12-day “Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires–Santiago” tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-iguazu-12-days/) includes Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain in Brazil, followed by Iguazu. **Iguazu is a nature stage, not a separate cultural and historical excursion**, so the Rio days are the right place to assess Brazil's cultural content on this option.

At [Iguazu's Brazilian side](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), check how much time is reserved for the park before the tour continues into Argentina. More time for Rio's museums, neighborhoods and music would require reallocating days, not an automatic expansion of every three-country itinerary.

## Santiago and Valparaíso: capital city and trading-port heritage

After Buenos Aires, the same 12-day route reaches Santiago. The Chile stage includes a trip to [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/). The combination introduces two distinct urban environments: a capital and a Pacific coastal port city.

UNESCO lists Valparaíso's historic quarter as World Heritage. Its architecture developed around international trade in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. Hills, stairs, funiculars and older neighborhoods tell the story of sea routes and migration. They deserve time for a full walk; a brief overview provides only an introduction.

The [13-day “Best of Brazil, Argentina and Chile” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-brazil-argentina-chile/) also includes Patagonia and Atacama, ending with Santiago and Maipo Valley. **This covers a wider geography**, but not necessarily the history of Chile's cities in greater depth: substantial time is spent on nature and transfers.

## Rapa Nui: when Chile becomes an archaeological destination

The [17-day Chile, Argentina and Brazil Grand Tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) includes Easter Island. Its cultural appeal goes beyond city sightseeing: Rapa Nui National Park is known for its moai stone figures and ahu ceremonial platforms.

According to UNESCO, the monuments embody a distinct Polynesian cultural tradition. **The island lies far from mainland Chile**, so visiting requires separate flights and overnight stays. Easter Island must not be presented as a mandatory stop on every journey that includes Chile.

The same 17-day program features Chilean wine areas, Atacama, Argentina's Mendoza, Buenos Aires and Iguazu. It combines several distinct experiences: Rapa Nui archaeology, capital-city culture and nature parks spread across different days. Choose it for this breadth of contrast, bearing in mind the time required.

## Flights between countries and actual time for sightseeing

The main challenge of combining Brazil and Chile is the distance between stops and the frequent inclusion of a third country. The 12-day program travels via Argentina. This means separate entry documents and payment arrangements for every country, while the Iguazu stage adds the Brazil–Argentina border crossing.

Rio has two important airports: international Galeão (GIG) and Santos Dumont (SDU). Near the falls, the Brazilian airport is IGU and the Argentine airport IGR. In Buenos Aires, distinguish EZE from AEP. Scheduling cultural sightseeing on the day of an airport change requires allowing for ground transport and formalities, not just flight time.
